historical_commentary.text: Dynamic menu management was a common requirement in 4D v6 applications, where the Design Mode Menu Bar Editor was the primary way to define menus, but runtime modification required procedural code. The specific issue described — that procedurally added menu items lack memory structures and associated methods — reflects limitations of the v6 menu system. Modern 4D provides a more flexible menu API and the ability to associate project methods with dynamically created menu items.
related_updates: 4D's menu management commands have been significantly expanded; dynamic menus can now be fully created and managed at runtime with associated methods
The menu bar architecture was modernized in later 4D versions with improved programmatic control
